# Deep Dive — What Happens When You Access a URL

[← Figma](../README.md) · [Every Figma question](../../figma.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/deep-dive-url-request-lifecycle)

`cs-fundamentals` `http` `networking` `open-ended`

---

## Requirements

This is an open-ended conversation: from the moment you enter a URL (like `www.example.com`) into a browser, walk through the entire process. Be prepared for deep dives on:

- DNS resolution and its inner workings.
- CDN and edge caching behavior.
- Service discovery — how services locate each other.
- Authentication.
- Inter-service communication protocols.

## Notes

- This round is truly open and unscripted — the questions may seem arbitrary, and the interviewer will probe deeper into whatever topics you bring up. Candidates who started with a wide scope often got cornered into specifics they couldn't handle.
- The best approach is to intentionally steer the discussion toward the subsystems you're most confident in and explore them thoroughly, rather than attempting to cover the entire stack superficially.

## Preparation

- Construct a single, well-reasoned story that traces the request lifecycle (DNS → TLS → routing/CDN → load balancing → service → database), and decide in advance which two or three areas you'll guide the conversation toward.
- Practice the most frequently examined topics — DNS resolution steps, CDN caching behavior, service discovery, and authentication token flow — until you can handle a series of follow-up questions with confidence.
